correctness.rationale: Assessed the corrected /workspace/repairs/3/RESULT.md. For a square-zero 3-by-3 map im lies in ker, so rank is at most one. XY and YX nonzero and proportional would force identical image and kernel for X and Y, making X and Y proportional and contradicting XY!=0. The two rank-four flag incidence bundles have closed images by projectivity of the respective bases and each is one-to-one over its independent-pair stratum, giving dimensions six and the two dense orbits in the Finding. The intersection minus zero is a punctured rank-two bundle over the three-dimensional complete flag variety; zero is in its closure. Linearization at (E12,E13) gives six coordinate zero equations, two diagonal-sum equations, and two independent mixed equations, with unit pivots in all characteristics. Transposition and basis permutation give the other generic case. At (E12,0) each of the square and mixed equations has rank four on its respective matrix variable; an invertible linear change of generators preserves the defining ideal and covers every proportional slope. The origin has no linear constraints. Thus the two six-dimensional components both have tangent dimension eight on their dense orbits; generic reducedness would give a smooth open in each after geometric base change. The explicit dual-number deformation maps (XY)[1,2] to -epsilon and detects a nonzero nilpotent. The frozen ancillary wording (line 63) calling this entry square-zero in the coordinate ring is false, not merely unproved: /workspace/review-replays/check_exterior_entry_square.py checked an integer linear functional annihilating all 4,617 products of the 27 defining quadrics with quadratic monomials but taking value 1 on ((XY)[1,2])^2. This certifies nonvanishing in every characteristic by scalar extension, while the entry is nilpotent by vanishing on geometric points. The corrected file drops only the erroneous square-zero attribution and clarifies the two stratum arguments. For the arithmetic statement each independent stratum has (q^2+q+1)|GL_2(F_q)| pairs; nonzero proportional pairs have (q^2+q+1)(q^2-1)(q+1) points by image line, nonzero covector, and slope. Adding zero and simplifying gives the claimed polynomial, and the two independent orbits, q+1 slopes and zero give q+4. The frozen enumeration was inspected, not executed; the arbitrary-field proof is independent of the two prime-field examples.
